section1_context:
bee is a Rust workspace that gives AI coding-agent tools capability-scoped access to a Linux host. Its security-critical path parses declarative policy, proves child-policy attenuation, resolves host identities and destinations, builds an eBPF-specific EnforcementPlan, attaches BPF LSM programs, creates a cgroup per scope, and enforces file-open, executable, and IP-connect decisions in the kernel. It also includes a higher-level harness for prompts, external model providers, built-in shell/file tools, local and remote MCP servers, transcripts/audit, CTF evaluation, in-process rendering, and work-in-progress SKILL.md discovery and grants.

The intended users are agent operators, framework integrators, and evaluation researchers. Production enforcement requires Linux BPF LSM/BTF/cgroup v2 and a privileged loader; the default harness build is only process-hardened and credential-stripped, not kernel-confined. The present analysis covers the dirty worktree, including uncommitted skill support. There is no database or multi-tenant service layer in this repository; the principal boundary is an untrusted or compromised model/tool workload running beneath a privileged same-host orchestrator.

section2_assets.asset: A1 — Provider API keys, MCP bearer tokens, and operator credentials
section2_assets.description: External-service authority, billing credentials, SSH/cloud secrets, and arbitrary sensitive files on the host.

section2_assets.asset: A2 — Host, harness process, and kernel enforcement integrity
section2_assets.description: Privileged orchestrator memory/environment, BPF programs/maps, cgroup membership, active LSM links, and surrounding host processes.

section2_assets.asset: A3 — Project source, artifacts, VCS metadata, and bee control-plane files
section2_assets.description: Real work product plus policy/scenario/provider/MCP/skill configuration that determines future behavior and authority.

section2_assets.asset: A4 — Sandbox policy, attenuation ceiling, executable identity, and consent decisions
section2_assets.description: The authoritative definition of allowed file, process, network, and tool capabilities.

section2_assets.asset: A5 — Network egress authority and downstream services
section2_assets.description: Model APIs, registries, remote MCP, internal endpoints, service mutations, and billable usage reachable from the host or scoped child.
section2_assets.sensitivity: Critical confidentiality, integrity, and economic value

section2_assets.asset: A6 — Prompts, model responses, tool data, skills, transcripts, metrics, and audit evidence
section2_assets.description: Potentially proprietary or secret interaction content and the evidence used to verify confinement.

section2_assets.asset: A7 — Harness availability and resource budget
section2_assets.description: CPU, memory, disk, audit capacity, provider tokens/cost, terminal state, and ability to launch confined work.

section2_assets.asset: A8 — CTF flags and evaluation/scoring integrity
section2_assets.description: Ground truth for adversarial evaluation and reproducible research results.

section3_entry_points.entry_point: E1 — CLI, environment, and host-side config/scenario materialization
section3_entry_points.description: CLI flags and TOML/YAML paths choose policies, parents, cgroup root, commands, workdirs/files, providers, endpoints, tokens, tools, skills, limits, and output paths; scenario files/directories are created before sandbox construction.
section3_entry_points.trust_boundary: operator or repository-controlled input -> privileged host process and filesystem

section3_entry_points.description: The harness sends prompts, tool schemas/results, and history to Anthropic or an OpenAI-compatible base URL; responses select tool names and arguments.
section3_entry_points.trust_boundary: local sensitive context and credential -> external provider -> tool dispatcher

section3_entry_points.entry_point: E3 — Built-in shell, process, and file tools
section3_entry_points.description: Model-controlled JSON invokes sh -c, cat, tee, ls, and other allowed binaries through either an enforced cgroup scope or host-only hardened mode.
section3_entry_points.trust_boundary: untrusted model output -> sandboxed child or launcher-user host authority

section3_entry_points.description: Config selects arbitrary executable/arguments/environment; the server speaks JSON-RPC and dynamically contributes tools. It is cgroup-scoped only in enforce builds.
section3_entry_points.trust_boundary: MCP config and third-party child process <-> harness registry/model conversation

section3_entry_points.description: A host-side client validates the authored hostname then connects using an optional bearer token; schemas, results, and list changes alter model-visible tools.
section3_entry_points.trust_boundary: trusted host credentials/network <-> remote server-controlled content and behavior

section3_entry_points.entry_point: E6 — Project/user skill discovery and invocation
section3_entry_points.description: Host-side code scans roots, parses YAML frontmatter, injects descriptions/bodies verbatim, applies project-over-user shadowing, and parses tool/filesystem grant requests.
section3_entry_points.trust_boundary: repository/user filesystem instructions -> trusted orchestrator and model behavior

section3_entry_points.description: Model-authored script is evaluated inside the harness process under explicit Rhai resource limits and a restricted drawing API.
section3_entry_points.trust_boundary: untrusted model script -> trusted harness address space

section3_entry_points.entry_point: E8 — Policy compilation, ambient resolution, attenuation, and planning
section3_entry_points.description: Policy input combines with cwd/HOME/PATH/DNS, protected defaults, parent-child subset logic, and fixed backend capabilities to produce map-ready rules.
section3_entry_points.trust_boundary: declarative authority and ambient host state -> kernel-installable policy

section3_entry_points.entry_point: E9 — Privileged loader, cgroup lifecycle, and BPF map installation
section3_entry_points.description: The host attaches global LSM hooks, creates scope cgroups, inserts map entries, moves children during pre_exec, consumes the audit map, and tears down cgroup directories.
section3_entry_points.trust_boundary: privileged userspace -> global kernel hooks and per-scope enforcement state

section3_entry_points.description: file_open, bprm_check_security, and socket_connect resolve runtime objects, consult cgroup-keyed maps, allow or deny, and reserve audit records.
section3_entry_points.trust_boundary: sandboxed process syscall -> kernel policy decision and audit stream

section3_entry_points.entry_point: E11 — Audit, transcript, metrics, and output persistence
section3_entry_points.description: Kernel records and model/tool exchanges are buffered, demultiplexed, correlated, serialized, printed, and written to operator-selected files.
section3_entry_points.trust_boundary: security-sensitive runtime data -> host memory/stdout/filesystem and downstream consumers

section3_entry_points.entry_point: E12 — Cargo/toolchain, GitHub Actions, and privileged VM test pipeline
section3_entry_points.description: Third-party actions, crates, rolling toolchains, bpf-linker, locally built artifacts, SSH tunnels, and sudo test runners build or validate a privileged security product.
section3_entry_points.trust_boundary: external supply chain and remote test infrastructure -> privileged release artifacts and VM root

vuln_table.title: Executable inode-pinning intent was silently downgraded to path-only enforcement
vuln_table.class: protection weakening and executable allowlist bypass
vuln_table.vector: An attacker able to replace a path-approved binary could run different code despite pin intent.
vuln_table.entry_point: E8 — Policy compilation, ambient resolution, attenuation, and planning

vuln_table.title: Enabled exfiltration protection was accepted but not enforced
vuln_table.class: missing security control and false assurance
vuln_table.vector: Sensitive reads could be combined with allowed egress even though policy requested exfiltration detection.
vuln_table.entry_point: E8 — Policy compilation, ambient resolution, attenuation, and planning

vuln_table.title: Policy validation did not mean the policy was runnable
vuln_table.class: incomplete validation and fail-late control deployment
vuln_table.vector: Review or CI could approve policy intent the backend could not install.
vuln_table.entry_point: E8 — Policy compilation, ambient resolution, attenuation, and planning
